vignette: Jamila had always been a pillar of strength in her community, serving as a police officer for over two decades. But that all changed on the fateful night she was assaulted while responding to a call. The memories of that evening still echoed vividly in her mind - the sound of shattering glass, the feel of hands around her throat, and the terror that gripped her heart. Even now, when she recalled those moments, she would hear the same sounds and feel the same fear coursing through her veins. As the days turned into weeks, Jamila began to notice that certain things would trigger a cascade of emotions and physical sensations. Whenever she drove with others, her heart would start racing, and she'd become hypervigilant, scanning the roads for potential threats. She'd see violence on TV or in the news, and suddenly she was back in that alleyway, fighting for her life. These triggers would send her spiraling into a vortex of negative thoughts and emotions. She began to believe that her body was betraying her, reacting as if she were still in danger even when she was safe at home. To cope with these feelings, Jamila started to isolate herself completely, cutting off all contact with friends and family. She'd tell herself it was for their own good - that she didn't want to burden them with her problems. But deep down, she knew it was because she couldn't rely on others; they hadn't been there to protect her when she needed them most. As she withdrew from the world, Jamila became increasingly vigilant, constantly monitoring her surroundings for potential threats and scrutinizing everyone she met. Her memories of that night continued to haunt her, vivid and unrelenting. She'd recall every detail - the smell of the alleyway, the taste of fear in her mouth, and the sound of her own screams. These recollections would bring back the same terror she felt at the time, leaving her breathless and shaken. Jamila couldn't shake the feeling that what happened to her was deeply unfair, that nothing had been done about it, and that justice had not been served. As time went on, these negative appraisals only intensified, fueling her maladaptive strategies. She became convinced that she was going crazy, constantly monitoring her thoughts for signs of slipping sanity. Her body felt like a traitor, reacting to every little thing as if it were a life-or-death situation. This constant state of hyperarousal left her exhausted and on edge. One day, while driving home from work, Jamila saw a group of teenagers gathered near the scene of her assault. Her heart started racing, and she felt herself slipping back into that vortex of fear and anxiety. She pulled over, gasping for air, and realized that she couldn't keep living like this. The weight of her memories, her negative appraisals, and her maladaptive strategies had become too much to bear. Jamila knew it was time to seek help, to confront the demons that haunted her and learn to live with herself again. For now, though, she remains trapped in this cycle of fear and avoidance, unsure of how to break free from the prison of her own mind.
